text: An issue with an active blocker context (set_project_issue_blocker_context) IS listed here even without a blocking link; the same rule drives the dependency graph and summary.

'blocked' is not a status accepted by update_issue (backlog|todo|in-progress|done|canceled): to mark a dependency, create a 'blocks' or 'is-blocked-by' link with create_issue_link; for an external blocker use set_project_issue_blocker_context.
Assigning work records an issue_assignee_changed activity visible to the team and fires an issue_updated webhook; confirm the person with the user unless the user named them.
Every assignment records an issue_assignee_changed activity visible to the team: show the assignment plan to the user before sending.
The issue then counts as blocked everywhere: dependency graph/summary, recommend_next_activity and list_blocked_project_issues (with or without a blocking link).
No background worker processes queued runs (runAnalyticsBridgeWorkerCycle exists but nothing calls it): the run stays 'queued' until process_analytics_bridge_run is called.

Lineage is normally attached when work is created from a materialized roadmap item (createIssueCommand reads workOrigin and roadmapLineageRefs, undeclared in the MCP schema); relinking is a governed roadmap change, so propose it to the owner instead of applying it (GOV-MAX).

Only visibility changes: archived projects are hidden from list_projects unless includeArchived=true (server.ts:37142), but project access checks ignore archived, so reads and writes on their issues still work.
It does not restore deleted data: delete_project removes the project recursively and cannot be undone.
Cheap call: one project document read plus a permission check (access.canManage).

idempotencyKey is an undeclared argument (API key only: the OAuth policy rejects unknown fields): with it the issue ID is derived from projectId+key and a replay with the same title returns the same ID (the text still says 'created').
Pick the active one by status=active; nothing prevents more than one active cycle.
Links carry only ids (sourceIssueId, targetIssueId): resolve titles with list_issues or get_issue.
Fetches the provider's model list (live API, or the built-in Vertex list when the server runs Gemini on Vertex), cached 5 minutes per workspace/provider/operation.
Changing models.embedding does not re-embed anything: stored embeddings stay from the old model until re-backfilled.
Runs are stored with a 30-day expiry (mcpBatch.ts:197); stored item results over 8000 chars are truncated on replay.
When userId and userEmail are both sent they are stored without cross-checking; with only userEmail the server looks the user up by email.
Only owner/admin can manage (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_ROLES); member and viewer are read-only. No pagination.
Owner-agent credentials (lpm_mcp_...) cannot call it: it is not in the roadmap-owner profile tool lists.
Immediate and irreversible: every client using the key then gets 'Invalid API key.' (server.ts:885-886). Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Also available to read-only API keys (it is a read tool outside SENSITIVE_ADMIN_TOOLS; src/lib/mcpToolCatalog.ts:633-635).
Archiving is permanent (archived principals are immutable, server.ts:17981) and immediately disables every MCP credential bound to the principal.
Slow: one synchronous call runs a code search and then an AI generation; connectors may abort long calls, so never loop it.
No pagination: returns every evidence record of the protocol (at most 20 per protocol, 100 MB in total).
The global LPM Help Center (e.g. 'boas-praticas-para-agentes') is served only by the web REST route /api/help-articles, not by MCP, so an empty list is normal.
Do not send undeclared fields such as executionGate: for non-repository jobs the server accepts a supplied executionGate.
Response can be ~11 MB of base64 (files up to 8 MiB); never paste it into chat.
The migration keeps the same reach: the new account policy allows only the host's original workspace and project and sets requiresTargeting = true (server.ts:21438-21441).

text: Unlike pause/resume, the coordinator fence is optional here (required only when one of coordinatorId, leaseNonce or fencingToken is sent).

Each call spends one search from the daily quotas: per credential (API key 500, OAuth grant 200, owner-agent credential its own limit) capped by the workspace daily cap (default 200, src/lib/genAppBuilderConfig.ts:37). Max 10 results.
Eligible = source/config/doc extensions (ts, js, py, java, go, md, json, yaml, sql, ...), at most 512 KB, outside node_modules/dist/build/vendor/coverage/secrets and not lock/min.js/map/.env files.
items=[] together with executiveContext=null means the workspace has no executive context yet (no gaps are computed), NOT that governance is complete.
The zip holds ALL data of the scope (flagged in the catalog as a data exfiltration risk); filters are stored but ignored by the export job (server.ts:4179).
With isCurrent=true the new current baseline starts EMPTY (requirements are copied only with cloneFromBaselineId, which this tool does not declare), so the approved scope shows zero requirements.
Large workspaces can exceed the 1 MB response cap (error, not truncation). Cached about 5 s per user (server.ts:8851).
In connectors this counts as a write call (roadmap:manage scope, so readOnlyHint is false) and may ask for confirmation.
'create' and 'materialize' types are effectively unusable here: preview requires existing item ids, and apply writes nothing for 'create' (server.ts:12767-12812).
